entries.title: Microphone: Always on or Push to talk
entries.how: Always on hears you whenever you are not muted; Push to talk hears you only while you press the mic. It is one setting, so the page and the app agree.
entries.about: Nothing leaves the Mac unless you hold the key or the button
iphone: ••• menu → Microphone → Always on / Push to talk
page: Settings → Microphone → Always on / Push to talk
the Always on / Hold to talk switch above the mic

entries.title: Talk button: hold or tap
entries.how: In push to talk, Hold to talk sends when you let go; Tap to talk starts with one tap and sends with the next. Each device keeps its own choice.
entries.about: Nothing leaves the Mac unless you hold the key or the button
iphone: ••• menu → Talk button → Hold to talk / Tap to talk
entries.iphone_note: Talk button shows in the menu once Microphone is Push to talk.
page: Settings → Microphone → Talk button → Hold to talk / Tap to talk

entries.title: Talk key and talking from any app
entries.how: On the page Space is the talk key, Caps Lock toggles talking, and a system-wide shortcut can run it from any app. On the iPhone the Action button, Back Tap or Siri ("Talk to Pointe") press it, and an AirPods stem press toggles it.
entries.about: Nothing leaves the Mac unless you hold the key or the button
page: Settings → Microphone → Talk key / System-wide shortcut

entries.title: Mute and unmute
entries.how: In Always on, the mic button in the middle mutes and unmutes you.
iphone: the mic button in the middle at the bottom (Mute / Unmute)
page: the mic button in the middle at the bottom (Microphone)
entries.page_note: Space, or a headset's play/pause button, mutes too while the page has focus.

entries.title: Hang up
entries.how: Hang up ends the call; your sessions keep running.
iphone: Hang up button at the bottom
page: Hang up button at the bottom

entries.title: Start a call
entries.how: Tap Connect to start the call on this device's microphone.

entries.title: Pair the iPhone with this Mac
entries.how: On the Mac's page, Settings → Phone → Connect your phone shows a code; scan it with the iPhone's Camera or in the Pointe app. The code works once and expires in 5 minutes.
entries.iphone_note: Pairing starts on the Mac's page: Settings → Phone → Connect your phone.

entries.title: Unpair a phone
entries.how: On the iPhone, Unpair this phone forgets the pairing there; the page's Settings → Phone lists the paired phones and removes them from the Mac. To pair again, show a new code there.

entries.title: Voice lock
entries.how: Voice lock learns your voice so other voices cannot approve or command. Enrol during a call, then pick a level: Off, Approvals, Commands or Everything.
entries.about: Only your voice counts, for approvals or for everything; checked on this Mac
page: Settings → Voice lock → Enrol my voice

entries.title: Wait before answering
entries.how: How long a pause ends your sentence: Quick answers as soon as you stop, Normal waits about a second, Patient waits longer.
iphone: ••• menu → Wait before answering → Quick / Normal / Patient
page: Settings → Turn taking → Wait before answering → Quick / Normal / Patient

entries.title: Don't interrupt me
entries.how: Say "don't interrupt me" or "hold on" and Pointe stays quiet until you say "go ahead" or "I'm done", or until 8 seconds of quiet.

entries.title: Appearance: light or dark
entries.how: Pick System, Light or Dark; System follows the device.
entries.page_note: The page keeps the choice in this browser.

entries.title: About and version
entries.how: About shows the version and that Pointe is open source (MIT).

entries.title: Brain dump
entries.how: Brain dump: talk freely while Pointe stays quiet; say "done" and it structures your words into a prompt you review and send.
entries.about: Dump your thoughts; Pointe structures them into a prompt in your words, and sends it only when you say
iphone: Brain dump button at the bottom
page: Brain dump button at the bottom

entries.title: Meeting mode
entries.how: Meeting mode sits in and takes notes, and stays quiet unless you let it speak. Nothing is sent to a session during it.
entries.about: Notes, lookups and a raised hand in a meeting, with consent and no sends
iphone: Start a meeting button at the top

entries.title: Challenge me
entries.how: Challenge argues against your plan one objection at a time and sends nothing; "verdict" ends it.
entries.about: The voice argues against your plan, grounded in your sessions, and cannot send

entries.title: Drive mode
entries.how: Drive mode gives short answers and approves by voice only what is safe from the road.
entries.about: Short answers, nothing to look at, and only safe requests approved by voice
iphone: ••• menu → Suggest Drive mode in the car
entries.page_note: The page has no Drive button: start it by voice or in the iPhone app.

entries.title: Whisper mode
entries.how: Whisper mode gives short, quiet replies for an open office; "back to normal" ends it.
entries.about: Quiet replies, a raised microphone, the same approval rules

entries.title: Briefing
entries.how: A briefing says what each session did, failed and waits on, most urgent first.
entries.about: "Brief me on the night": what each session did, failed and waits on

entries.title: Scheduled briefing
entries.how: A scheduled briefing is read on the Mac at the time and days you pick.

entries.title: Dictionary
entries.how: Correct a misheard word in the conversation and Pointe learns it; the Dictionary lists, adds and edits terms. A new term applies from the next call.
entries.about: Fix a misheard name once, and the next call hears it right

entries.title: Alerts and the Apple Watch
entries.how: Alerts tell you when a session needs you; Approve from notifications adds Approve on the iPhone and Apple Watch.
entries.about: A session needs you: the watch taps, the desktop notifies
page: Settings → Alerts → Desktop alerts while this tab is in the background / Approve from notifications (iPhone and Apple Watch)

entries.title: Conflict alarm
entries.how: The conflict alarm says when two sessions claim opposite things about the same work; it can be spoken or a card only.
entries.about: Two sessions claim opposite things about the same work: you hear it at once
page: Settings → Conflict alarm → Check sessions against each other

entries.title: Show while it says
entries.how: Show while it says puts the file, diff or failing test on screen as the voice mentions it. On the Mac it is always on; on the phone you turn it on.
entries.about: The file, diff or failing test appears on screen as the voice mentions it
page: Settings → Show while it says → Also show on the phone

entries.title: Clean up my words
entries.how: Clean up my words shows, under each thing you say, a clean version of what the voice understood.
page: Clean up my words at the top

entries.title: Orchestrator or session mode
entries.how: Orchestrator mode sends each request to the session it is about; session mode sends everything to the active session.
iphone: Sessions button at the bottom → Orchestrator / Session
page: Orchestrator / Session in the Sessions panel on the left

entries.title: Switch session
entries.how: Say "switch to" and the session's name, or tap it.
iphone: long-press a session at the top → Focus on this session
entries.iphone_note: Or tap its chip at the top.
entries.page_note: Click the session in the Sessions panel on the left.

entries.title: Rename a session
entries.how: Say "rename this to" and the new name, or rename it on screen.
iphone: long-press a session at the top → Rename
page: hover a session in the Sessions panel (on touch, its ⋯) → Rename

entries.title: Close a session
entries.how: Say "close" and the session's name (or "close all except …"): it leaves the voice and keeps running in its terminal.
iphone: long-press a session at the top → Disconnect from the voice
Sessions button at the bottom → Disconnect
entries.iphone_note: In the Sessions sheet, swipe a session left.
page: hover a session in the Sessions panel (on touch, its ⋯) → Disconnect from the voice

entries.title: Add a session
entries.how: Run /pointe:voice in a Claude Code session, or pointe join opencode in its folder, and it joins the voice.

entries.title: Other machines
entries.how: Sessions on your other Macs and Linux machines join through a small Pointe there: invite the machine and run pointe node join with the code.

entries.title: Type instead of talking
entries.how: Type sends written words to the voice, for a noisy room or a quiet one.

entries.title: Approve or deny a request
entries.how: When a session asks permission, Pointe reads it out: say yes or no, or tap on its card.

entries.title: Where the settings are
entries.how: All settings are in one place on each surface.
entries.iphone_note: The ••• button at the top right.
page: Settings in the Sessions panel on the left
entries.page_note: On a narrow window, open the Sessions button first.

entries.title: Update Pointe
entries.how: In a terminal: claude plugin marketplace update pointe, then claude plugin update pointe@pointe, then /pointe:stop and /pointe:voice so the voice restarts on the new version. The iPhone app is built from source: build and install it again from Xcode.
